classification.difficultyReason: Across three unpartitioned geometric configurations, trace linked equality and multiple parallel-direction families, transfer opposite/alternate angles, identify complementary and junction-angle relations, and apply diagonal bisection without intermediate prompts. These combined choices exceed a single routine substitution, while each theorem is explicitly taught.

content.prompt: Use the properties of a parallelogram to find the values of $x,y,z,\alpha$, and $\beta$ in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Four parallelograms share one vertex. Preserve the central right angle, equality ticks and three parallel-direction families. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Opposite sides and angles of parallelograms; matched vertical sides; complementary central angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides of the upper-left parallelogram are equal, so its right side has length $10$. The matching ticks transfer this length to the left side of the lower-right parallelogram. Its opposite side gives $y=10$.

The central angle of the lower-left parallelogram equals the opposite $70^\circ$ angle of the upper-right parallelogram, using the marked parallel directions. Hence $\alpha=70^\circ$.

In the upper-left parallelogram, the angle between the upward vertical ray and the upper-left sloping ray at the centre is $70^\circ$ (opposite angles). The marked perpendicular directions give
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=90^\circ-70^\circ\\\beta&=20^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three parallelograms share edges around one junction; single, double and triple arrows identify the three direction families.
spec.mathematics: Opposite sides equal; adjacent angles supplementary; angles around the shared junction total 360 degrees.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides of each parallelogram are equal. The central steep side equals $5$, so $x=5$. The shared near-horizontal side equals $7$, so $y=7$. The lower-right oblique side equals the segment marked $3$, so $z=3$.

Adjacent angles in the right parallelogram are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-80^\circ\\\beta&=100^\circ.\end{align*}$$
At the central junction, the left parallelogram contributes $130^\circ$ and the right parallelogram contributes $80^\circ$, by opposite angles. Angles at a point give
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=360^\circ-130^\circ-80^\circ\\\alpha&=150^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram with both diagonals, their source extensions, external angle labels and offset dimension arrows for the two halves of the descending diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Diagonals bisect; parallel sides give corresponding and alternate angles; exterior angles are supplementary.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so $x=3$.

The angle between the top side and the rising diagonal inside the upper-right vertex is $50^\circ$ (alternate angles, top and bottom sides parallel). Thus
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\\alpha&=130^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The interior angle between the left side and descending diagonal at the upper-left vertex is $180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ$. The left and right sides are parallel, so alternate angles give $\beta=70^\circ$.
